Re: Motion to Intervene in Docket No. 59475, Bell County East to Big Hill 765 kV
Transmission Line Project, SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349


Dear Commissioners and Presiding Officer:

Pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code § 22.104 and other applicable rules and statutes, I
respectfully file this Motion to Intervene in the above-referenced proceeding.

I. Identification of Movant

My name is Brant Myers. I am a resident of Brady, McCulloch County, Texas, and I currently
lease the property identified in this proceeding as Tract Nos. 4226, 4229, and 4230, under a
lease agreement with the landowner, Bonnie Oswald Brotherton. I am also the ranch manager
for the aforementioned tracts/property.

II. Prior Participation

I previously submitted comments as a protester (Interchange Item 1417), expressing my
opposition and concerns regarding the proposed Bell County East to Big Hill 765 kV
Transmission Line Project - in specific regard to Link V8.

III. Basis for Intervention

I have a direct and substantial interest in the outcome of this proceeding because I am the
ranch manager and current lessee actively occupying and using the land. I run cattle on the
leased land as part of my agricultural operations.

The proposed project would materially and adversely affect my leasehold interest and
day-to-day use of the property in the following ways:


                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475​
                                                               SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
            ○​ Loss or fragmentation of grazing pasture;
           ○​ Potential disruption to cattle movement and access to water sources;
           ○​ Increased risk of injury to livestock from construction activities or proximity to
              infrastructure;
           ○​ Reduction in the productive use and economic value of the leased property;
           ○​ Noise, dust, and other construction disturbances that could stress the herd and
              impact my livelihood.

The landowner, Bonnie Oswald Brotherton, is unable to intervene in this matter or
actively participate due to significant family health circumstances. Her husband is
suffering from a terminal illness. She is his primary caregiver, and they live several hours
away.

As a result, I am requesting to be moved to intervenor status as a member of the V8
Landowner’s Coalition in order to represent the interests of the leased property in this
proceeding. (Confirmation letter from the V8 Landowners Coalition uploaded with this
filing as an attachment.)
My interests as ranch manager and lessee are not adequately represented by any other party.
Granting me intervenor status will allow the Commission to receive important information
regarding the real-world impacts of the proposed project on individuals who actually live on and
work the land.

Intervention will not unduly complicate, delay, or prejudice this proceeding. I accept the
procedural schedule, discovery deadlines, and record exactly as they exist at the time of
this filing.

IV. Request for Relief

For the foregoing reasons, I respectfully request that the Commission or the presiding
Administrative Law Judge grant this Motion to Intervene and recognize me as a full intervenor
as a member of the V8 Landowners Coalition with all rights and responsibilities of a party in this
docket.

I certify that a copy of this Motion has been served on all parties of record via the Commission’s
Interchange system on the date below.

Respectfully submitted,

Brant Myers

Re: PUC Docket No. 59475 – Application of V8 Transmission, LLC for a Certificate of
Convenience and Necessity for the Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV Transmission Line
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349

To Whom It May Concern / Presiding Administrative Law Judge:

The V8 Landowners Coalition hereby confirms and accepts Brant Myers as a member of the
V8 Landowners Coalition for purposes of intervention in the above-referenced proceeding.

Mr. Brant Myers manages and leases property (Tract Nos. 4226, 4229, 4230) owned by Bonnie
Oswald Brotherton in McCulloch County, Texas, which is directly affected by the proposed
transmission line route. Due to Ms. Brotherton’s full-time caregiving responsibilities for her
husband who is terminally ill, Mr. Meyers represents the interests of the leased property in this
matter as ranch manager and lessee.

The V8 Landowners Coalition has no objection to Mr. Myers intervention in this docket as a
member of the Coalition. We support his participation and authorize him to align with and be
represented through the Coalition’s positions, filings, and legal representation where
appropriate. Mr. Myers may also file supplemental testimony or evidence if needed to address
specific impacts to his leasehold interest.

We respectfully request that the Commission and Administrative Law Judge grant Mr. Brant
Myers intervenor status in PUC Docket No. 59475.

Sincerely,
